answer: The ploughman counts every furrow he turns, and the parish tally book holds the count for each field he works through the season. A bridge tally copied from another farm fails at once: at the signal of the field the furrows must run straight and even, and a copied count never matches the ground. Faking a season means hiring a plough team for four months, feeding two oxen and paying 7,400 in wages and feed, while the pulse entry in the tally book is read at every rent day, so a field whose furrows were never counted is struck from the roll.
